task_message:
Case M14: segment the myxoid soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 220x220x300 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Case M14 is complete.

**What I segmented:** a well-circumscribed, markedly T2-hyperintense, lobulated soft-tissue mass at the myofascial/subcutaneous junction of the (posterolateral) limb, measuring ~3.3 × 2.9 × 5.4 cm — consistent with a myxoid soft-tissue tumor.

**How I got there:**
- Surveyed the volume with axial/coronal/sagittal contact sheets; identified the round/ovoid bright mass and distinguished it from the large saturated rectangular structure at the FOV edge (a skin-surface marker/reference, not tumor) and from vessels/fascial fluid planes.
- Seeded with a single positive point at the lesion core (v1, 20.1 mL), verified the outline in all three planes and found slight under-coverage anteriorly/inferiorly.
- Accepted the one automatic candidate that represented true lesion periphery (C2, +7.0 mL → v2) and ran a model refine to smooth the intensity-based boundary (v3, 26.3 mL, single connected component).
- At final review, confirmed the outline follows the lesion border on all panels, that the slices just past each end are free of lesion tissue, and rejected the remaining candidates (C1/C2/C3/C4/C5) as fat-plane/vessel clutter.

Final mask: v3, 26.3 mL, 1 component. Confidence: medium (fuzzy periphery and a thin superior pole tracking along the fascia).
